mainTopic: A נזירה whose husband annulled her vow, and the four rams of a נזיר brought without bread
overview: This amud continues the משנה about a married woman who set aside animals for her נזירות offerings before her husband annulled her vow. רבא explains that even according to רבנן, the husband transfers the animal to her only for what she needs, so after the annulment it is not holy. The גמרא then asks how a married woman can own her own animal at all. רב פפא answers that she saved from her food, and a second answer is that someone gave it to her on condition that her husband has no rights in it. Next, שמואל challenges אבוה בר איהי to explain a ברייתא listing four rams of a נזיר that come without bread: his, hers, after death, and after atonement. The גמרא explains each one. 'Hers' is our משנה, and 'his' is a father who made his son a נזיר. The ram after death comes from a ברייתא, and the ram after atonement is learned by logic, since neither can bring atonement. The גמרא asks why the list leaves out a שלמים slaughtered שלא כמצותן, and answers that the list only counts offerings brought properly. Finally it returns to the ruling about a dead נזיר's unspecified money in order to discuss it.

steps.title: רבא: the husband only transfers what his wife needs
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that even according to רבנן, the husband transfers ownership of the animal to his wife only for what she actually needs to bring.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: You can even say the משנה follows the רבנן. When the husband transfers the animal to her, he does so only for something she needs. For something she does not need, he does not transfer it to her.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new explanation for why the husband's animal goes back to being an ordinary animal after he annuls her vow. He says even the רבנן can agree with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The husband gave his wife the animal only so she could bring her required offerings. Once he annuls her vow, she no longer needs them, so the transfer never really took hold for this purpose. That is why the animal is not holy and can go graze with the flock.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say (this fits even the opinion of...)
The Sages, the majority opinion
He transfers ownership
It is needed by her

phrases.english: Rava said: You can even say it follows the Rabbis,
since even when he transfers it to her,
phrases.notes: "He" is the husband, and "it" is the animal he gave her for her offerings.

phrases.english: it is for a matter that she needs;

phrases.aramaic: בְּמִילְּתָא דְּלָא צְרִיכָא לַהּ — לָא מַקְנֵי לַהּ.
phrases.english: for a matter she does not need, he does not transfer it to her.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues from the previous discussion and gives a different explanation of the משנה's ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the scope of the husband's transfer of ownership
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ruling seemed to fit only one particular opinion.
steps.terutzMaskana: Even רבנן agree, because the husband only transfers the animal for what the wife needs. After the annulment she does not need it.
steps.whatToRemember: The husband's gift to his wife has a built-in limit: it only covers what she actually needs.

steps.title: How can a married woman own her own animal?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's case of an animal belonging to the woman, and asks how she could own anything, since whatever a wife acquires belongs to her husband.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: If the animal was hers, the חטאת must be left to die and the עולה is offered. But where would she get her own property? Didn't you say that whatever a woman acquires, her husband acquires?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה and immediately challenges it. How can a married woman have an animal that is truly her own?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a known rule that anything a married woman acquires automatically goes to her husband. If so, the משנה's case of 'her own animal' seems impossible. The גמרא needs to find a case where she really owns it.

keyTerms.meaning: Sin-offering
It must be left to die
Burnt-offering
From where does she have it?
Whatever a wife acquires, her husband acquires

phrases.english: If her animal was her own,
the sin-offering must die, and the burnt-offering is offered.
She, from where does she have her own?
But didn't you say: whatever a woman acquires,
her husband acquires!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next clause of the משנה and challenges its basic case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of an animal that belongs to the wife
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A married woman's acquisitions belong to her husband, so she cannot own an animal of her own.

steps.title: רב פפא: she saved from her dough
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא answers that she bought the animal with money she saved by cutting back from her own food.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: It is a case where she saved it up from her dough.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא gives a case where the wife really does own the animal. She saved money by eating less of the food given to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Money saved from a wife's own food allowance is considered hers, not her husband's. So an animal bought with those savings can truly belong to her, and the משנה's case makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: She saved it up by cutting back
Her dough (her food portion)

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Where she saved it from her dough.
phrases.notes: He means she ate less and used what she saved to buy the animal.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: A married woman cannot own anything of her own.
steps.terutzMaskana: Savings from her own food portion are hers.

steps.title: Another answer: a gift with a condition
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: someone else gave her the animal on the condition that her husband has no rights in it.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you wish, say: Another person gave it to her and told her, 'On condition that your husband has no rights in it.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a second way a married woman can own property. An outsider gave it to her and specifically shut the husband out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The giver can set conditions on his own gift. If he says the husband gets no rights, the animal belongs only to the wife. So the משנה's case of 'her animal' is possible this way too.

keyTerms.meaning: If you wish, say (an alternate answer)
Another person transferred it to her
On condition that
Rights, control

phrases.english: If you wish, say:
that another person transferred it to her,
and he said to her:
"On condition that your husband has no rights in them."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Everything a wife gets goes to her husband.
steps.terutzMaskana: A giver can exclude the husband, making the gift hers alone.
steps.whatToRemember: Two ways a married woman can own her own animal: savings from her food, or a gift that excludes the husband.

steps.title: שמואל's challenge: the four rams without bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's ruling that the עולה and שלמים are offered, and שמואל demands that אבוה בר איהי explain a ברייתא listing four rams that are brought without bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: The עולה is offered as an עולה, and the שלמים are offered, etc. שמואל said to אבוה בר איהי: Don't sit down on your feet until you explain this to me: These are four rams that do not need bread: his, hers, after death, and after atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the משנה's next ruling about the שלמים. שמואל uses it to challenge אבוה בר איהי to explain a ברייתא about four special rams. This sets up the explanation that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a נזיר's שלמים ram comes with loaves of bread. The ברייתא lists four cases where the ram is brought without bread. שמואל wants each of the four cases explained.

keyTerms.meaning: Peace-offering
Don't sit down on your feet (until you answer)
Rams
Require bread to come with them
Atonement

phrases.english: The burnt-offering is offered as a burnt-offering,
and the peace-offering is offered, etc.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ שְׁמוּאֵל לַאֲבוּהּ בַּר אִיהִי:
phrases.english: Shmuel said to Avuh bar Ihi:
Do not sit down on your feet
until you tell me this matter:
And these are four rams
that do not require bread:
his, and hers,
and the one after death, and the one after atonement.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תִּיתֵּיב עַל כַּרְעָיךְ עַד דְּאָמְרַתְּ לִי הָדָא מִילְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next clause of the משנה and brings in a related ברייתא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What are the four cases of a ram brought without bread?

steps.title: 'Hers' is our משנה's case
steps.stepSummary: The first item, 'hers', refers to the case just discussed: a woman's own animal after her husband annulled her vow.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'Hers' — that is what we just said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts explaining the list. 'Hers' is the case of our משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה is about a woman who set aside her own animal and then her vow was annulled. Her שלמים ram is brought, but without bread.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we said

phrases.english: Hers: this is what we said.
phrases.notes: This points back to our משנה: the woman whose husband annulled her vow after she set aside her own animal.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering שמואל's question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'Hers' is the woman's animal from our משנה.

steps.title: 'His' is a father who made his son a נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The second item, 'his', comes from a משנה: a father can make his young son a נזיר, but if the son shaves or protests, the nazirite status ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'His' — as we learned: A man can make his son a נזיר, but a woman cannot make her son a נזיר. If the son shaved, or relatives shaved him, if he protested, or relatives made him protest...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains 'his' by quoting a משנה about a father who makes his young son a נזיר. The quote continues in the next step, which reaches the line about the ram without bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only a father, not a mother, can place a nazirite vow on a young son. The son can cancel it by shaving or by protesting, either on his own or pushed by relatives. This sets up a case where an animal set aside for the boy's offerings is left over.

keyTerms.meaning: As we learned in a משנה
Places a vow upon
He shaved
He protested
Relatives

steps.confusionAlert: 'His' here does not mean the husband's animal from our משנה. It means the father's case: a man who made his son a נזיר.

phrases.english: His: as we learned:
A man can vow his son to be a nazirite,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין הָאִשָּׁה מַדֶּרֶת אֶת בְּנָהּ בְּנָזִיר.
phrases.english: but a woman cannot vow her son to be a nazirite.
If he shaved, or relatives shaved him,
phrases.notes: "He" is the young son, showing he doesn't want to be a נזיר.

phrases.english: if he protested, or relatives made him protest.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues explaining the list from step 5, moving to the second item.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'His' is the case of a father who made his son a נזיר and the son canceled it.

steps.title: The father's leftover money: the peace-offering is brought without bread
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה about a father who made his son a נזיר. If the money was assigned to a שלמים, that שלמים is brought but needs no bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had money that was not assigned to a specific offering, it goes to communal gift offerings. If the money was assigned: the sin-offering money is thrown into the Dead Sea. The burnt-offering money buys a burnt-offering, and someone who benefits from it is liable for misuse. The peace-offering money buys a peace-offering, which is eaten for one day and does not need bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting the משנה from Step 7. That משנה ends with the case that proves the second ram, 'his', is brought without bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The father set aside money for his son's נזיר offerings, but the son's נזירות ended. Each type of money goes to its own place. The key line is the last one: the שלמים is brought but needs no bread. This is the ram on the list called 'his', meaning the father's.

keyTerms.meaning: Money set aside for נזירות offerings in general, not assigned to any specific offering
Money assigned to a specific offering
A gift offering; here, communal gift offerings bought with the leftover money
The Dead Sea, where money is thrown so no one can use it
Misuse of הקדש, which makes a person liable

steps.whyThisMatters: This completes the proof for the second ram on the list of four.

phrases.english: If he had unallocated money,
phrases.notes: 'He' is the father from Step 7, who set aside money for his son's nazirite offerings.

phrases.english: it goes to gift offerings.
If it was allocated money:
the money for a sin-offering goes to the Dead Sea,
phrases.notes: In other words, it is thrown away where nobody can use it.

phrases.english: with the money for a burnt-offering they bring a burnt-offering,
and one is liable for misuse with it.
with the money for a peace-offering they bring a peace-offering,
and it is eaten for one day,
and it does not require bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quotation of the משנה begun in Step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The father's שלמים, bought with money set aside for his son's נזירות, is brought without bread.

steps.title: Where do we learn the ram after death?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא moves to the third ram on the list, the one brought after the owner's death, and asks for its source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ram brought after death: where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the source of the third ram on the list. This question sets up the ברייתא quoted next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא from Step 5 listed a ram brought after the owner's death as needing no bread. The גמרא wants a text that says so.

keyTerms.meaning: Where do we know it from?
After death, meaning the ram is offered after the נזיר has died

phrases.english: The one after death: from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the second item to the third item on the list.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that a נזיר's ram offered after his death needs no bread.

steps.title: The ברייתא begins: general money set aside for נזירות
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It starts with the rule for general נזירות money: one may not benefit from it, but there is no liability for מעילה, since all of it could be used for שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: someone who sets aside money for his נזירות may not benefit from it, but if he does, he is not liable for misuse. This is because all of it could be used to bring peace-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts quoting a ברייתא to answer the question. This opening part lays the background, and the case of death comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Unassigned נזירות money is forbidden to use. Still, there is no liability for מעילה, because all of it could end up as שלמים, and שלמים does not carry that liability at this stage. This sets the background for what happens if the נזיר dies.

keyTerms.meaning: As it is taught in a ברייתא
One who sets aside
Benefiting from or using something

phrases.english: As it is taught:
One who separates money for his naziriteship:
one may not benefit from it, but one is not liable for misuse with it,
because it is fit
to bring peace-offerings with all of it.
phrases.notes: Peace-offerings don't carry misuse liability at this stage, so this money doesn't either.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the answer to Step 9's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: This part sets up the ברייתא. The actual case of death appears in the next step.

steps.title: If the נזיר died, his peace-offering is brought without bread
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: if the נזיר died, each type of money goes to its place, and his שלמים is brought and eaten for one day without bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he died and had unallocated money, it goes to gift offerings. If the money was allocated: the sin-offering money goes to the Dead Sea, and one may not benefit from it, but there is no liability for misuse. The burnt-offering money buys a burnt-offering, and there is liability for misuse. The peace-offering money buys a peace-offering, which is eaten for one day and does not need bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא now gives the case of a נזיר who died. It says outright that his שלמים needs no bread, which proves the third ram.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after the owner's death, his שלמים is still offered, but without the bread that normally goes with a נזיר's ram. This is the explicit source for the ram 'after death'.

keyTerms.meaning: He died
He takes it (to the Dead Sea)
Eaten for only one day, unlike a regular שלמים, which may be eaten for two days
Require bread, meaning the loaves that normally come with a נזיר's ram

steps.whatToRemember: A נזיר's ram brought after his death is offered without bread. This is stated outright in a ברייתא.

phrases.english: If he died and had unallocated money,
it goes to gift offerings.
If it was allocated money:
the money for a sin-offering, he takes it to the Dead Sea;
one may not benefit from it, but one is not liable for misuse.
With the money for a burnt-offering they bring a burnt-offering,
and one is liable for misuse with it.
With the money for a peace-offering they bring a peace-offering,
and it is eaten for one day,
and it does not require bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from Step 10 and reaches the case that answers Step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A dead נזיר's שלמים is brought without bread.

steps.title: The ram after atonement is learned by logic
steps.stepSummary: For the fourth ram, the one brought after atonement, the גמרא needs no text. It uses logic: the ram after death needs no bread because it cannot bring atonement, and the same is true of a ram brought after atonement.
steps.simpleTranslation: The ram brought after atonement is known by logic. Why does the ram after death need no bread? Because it is not fit to bring atonement. A ram brought after atonement also cannot bring atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the fourth ram on the list by comparing it to the third. This finishes explaining all four rams.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The reason the ram after death needs no bread is that it no longer brings atonement. A ram brought after the owner already got atonement with a different animal has the same feature. So the same rule applies, and no separate source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Atonement; here, the offering that completes the נזירות
Logical reasoning
What is the reason?
Fit or suitable

steps.whatToRemember: All four rams are now explained: 'hers', 'his', after death, and after atonement. The last two need no bread because they cannot bring atonement.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows the reason behind leaving out the bread for the last two rams: once an offering cannot bring atonement, the bread is not brought with it.

phrases.english: The one after atonement is known by logic.
phrases.notes: This is the fourth ram: brought after the owner already got atonement through a different animal.

phrases.english: The one after death: what is the reason?
Because it is not fit for atonement.
The one after atonement too:
it is not fit for atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ram after death from Step 11 as the model for the ram after atonement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ram after atonement needs no bread because, like the ram after death, it cannot bring atonement.

steps.title: Isn't there another ram with no bread?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the list leaves out a נזיר's שלמים slaughtered שלא כמצותן, which also needs no bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really all? There is another case: any other שלמים of a נזיר that were slaughtered not the proper way are valid, but they don't count toward the owner's obligation. They are eaten for one day and need neither bread nor the foreleg!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the list of rams that need no bread. It points to another case that seems to belong on the list but is missing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A נזיר's שלמים slaughtered שלא כמצותן is still a kosher קרבן. It is eaten for one day like a נזיר's שלמים, yet it needs no bread and no זרוע. If the list is supposed to cover every ram that comes without bread, this case should be on it.

keyTerms.meaning: "And is there nothing more?" Asks whether a list is really complete.
Not the proper way it is supposed to be done
Do not count for the owner as fulfilling his obligation
The foreleg of the ram, normally given to the כהן
Require

steps.confusionAlert: "Valid" (כשרים) does not mean the נזיר is finished. The קרבן is kosher and eaten, but he still has to bring another one for his obligation.

phrases.english: And is there nothing more?
But isn't there this:
And all other peace-offerings of a nazir
that he slaughtered not according to their מצוה
are valid,
but they do not count for the owner as his obligation,
and they are eaten for one day,

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵינָן טְעוּנִין לֹא לֶחֶם וְלֹא זְרוֹעַ!
phrases.english: and they require neither bread nor the foreleg!
phrases.notes: The foreleg is the cooked piece the כהן normally gets from a נזיר's ram.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After all four rams on the list have been given sources, the גמרא asks whether the list is missing a case.
steps.kashyaTarget: The completeness of the list of rams that need no bread.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A שלמים slaughtered שלא כמצותן also needs no bread, so a complete list should include it.

steps.title: The list only counts offerings brought properly
steps.stepSummary: The list counts only offerings brought according to their מצוה, so the שלא כמצותן case was left out on purpose.
steps.simpleTranslation: The list counts offerings done the proper way. It does not count offerings that were not done the proper way.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by explaining what kind of cases the list covers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All four rams on the list were brought correctly, and they still need no bread. A ram slaughtered the wrong way is a different kind of case, so leaving it off does not make the list incomplete. The list was never meant to include mistakes.

keyTerms.meaning: He counts / includes in the list
According to their מצוה, done properly

steps.whatToRemember: The list of rams with no bread only covers rams brought properly. A ram slaughtered שלא כמצותן also has no bread, but it is outside the list.

phrases.english: He counts those done according to their מצוה;
phrases.notes: "He" is the תנא who made the list.

phrases.english: those not done according to their מצוה he does not count.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the list
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The list was meant to include every ram of a נזיר that comes without bread.
steps.terutzMaskana: The list only includes rams brought properly, so the שלא כמצותן case does not belong.
steps.triggerLanguage: כְּמִצְוָתָן קָא חָשֵׁיב, שֶׁלֹּא כְּמִצְוָתָן לָא קָא חָשֵׁיב

steps.title: Back to the dead נזיר's unspecified money
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the earlier ruling that a dead נזיר's unspecified money goes to נדבה, so it can examine that ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he had unspecified money, it goes to gift offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up its next discussion. It goes back to a line from the earlier ruling about a נזיר who died, so it can discuss that line next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a נזיר set aside money without saying which קרבן it was for, and then he died, that money is used for communal gift offerings (נדבה). The גמרא repeats this line on purpose, because the next part of the daf will analyze it.

keyTerms.meaning: Unspecified money, set aside without saying which קרבן it is for
It goes to communal gift offerings
A voluntary gift offering

phrases.english: If he had unspecified money,
phrases.notes: This goes back to the case of a נזיר who set aside money and then died.

phrases.english: it goes to gift offerings,

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיוּ לוֹ מָעוֹת סְתוּמִים יִפְּלוּ לִנְדָבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the list of rams and goes back to the earlier ruling about money of a נזיר who died.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Unspecified money of a נזיר who died is used for communal gift offerings.
